newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Nedlloyd says 10 pct return on capital realistic.
newsitem.headline: Nedlloyd says 10 pct return on capital realistic.

text.p: Dutch transport and shipping group Koninklijke Nedlloyd Groep NV Groep NV believes its return on capital can jump to 10 percent if its merger with P&O goes ahead, chief financial officer Haddo Meijer told Reuters Financial Television on Thursday.

"We believe that through (the merger with P&O), plus a further strengthening of our focus of the transportation business we have in Europe, that the 10 percent return (on capital employed) objective is achievable," he said.
In 1995, Nedlloyd's operating result was 5.5 percent of average capital employed.
Initial estimates of $200 million in savings in the short to mid-term from the merger remained realistic.
"That is a likely figure. The ambition is to implement that in a relatively short period of time, about 18 months... The merger is really on track in this respect," said Meijer.
Debt would also be under control, he said.

"We don't have a sizeable debt burden... After we have implemented the merger as per January 1, we will be at a solvency ratio for Royal Nedlloyd of 45 percent, group equity expressed in total assets of 45 percent and debt-to-equity will amount to 60 percent. So we are in a very healthy situation."

The outlook for Nedlloyd's other major activity, road haulage in northwest Europe, was also promising, Meijer said. He explained that Germany remained the key to the business and that its Unitrans operations there were recovering.

"We expect for the fourth quarter that Unitrans will be in black figures. So we (have) solved the situation we had in the past. That is very important because we believe that Germany is very important in view of the strategy we want to build in the European transportation sector. Without Germany, you don't have a position," he said.
On Wednesday, Nedlloyd announced a drop of third quarter net profits of 38 percent. However, discounting asset sales last year, the ordinary net profit rose from 19 million to 36 million guilders.

On Thursday, the European Commission said it was probing the proposed merger between Nedlloyd and Peninsula and Oriental Steam Navigation Co (P&O). The Commission has until December 19 to decide whether to clear the merger or begin an in-depth four month investigation.
